# Phase Two — Critique and Improvements

The Awtsmoos gives Gevurah to guard the work from its own ambition; Awtsmoos.com improves when breadth never becomes blindness.

## Improvements

1. Do not equate HTML-file count with public-route count; classify fixtures/templates first.
2. Do not wait on full `git status` before route discovery; keep a lighter census lane.
3. Do not rewrite actively claimed routes even when screenshots look terrible.
4. Use prior agent outputs as evidence but refresh critical claims from current files/runtime.
5. Finish Sefarim tests before using it as a design precedent.
6. Browser-test Sefarim because source/test green still cannot prove layout.
7. Avoid generic Lighthouse-like scores as the sole performance gate; collect actionable timing/resource evidence.
8. Measure interactive readiness for games/editors, not only DOMContentLoaded.
9. Separate site-owned console errors from browser extensions/noise.
10. Treat 404s for intentional optional resources differently from broken required assets.
11. Detect page-level horizontal overflow and internal intentional scrollers separately.
12. Check 200% zoom on representative interactive families.
13. Prefer native disclosure/buttons/forms over custom JS controls when semantics allow.
14. Preserve route-local visual identity; coherence should come from interaction quality, not identical styling.
15. Avoid adding new dependencies for cosmetic fixes.
16. Version changed static assets when the current cache model requires query versions.
17. Inspect compact server implementation before adding query params to assets.
18. Compare compact response latency as well as bytes; CPU-heavy transforms can make small files slower.
19. Check caching/content-encoding before merging CSS modules just to reduce request count.
20. Keep tests about user-visible invariants, not obsolete DOM implementation trivia.
21. Add regression contracts only after the first implementation draft for each route.
22. Rerun scoped status immediately before each production write.
23. Record route owner/claim evidence in the ledger.
24. Use sitewide reruns between tranches to catch regressions early.
25. Do not publish until secret/large-file/risk checks pass.
26. Push all safe requested unrelated changes, but never knowingly publish credentials or machine-local secrets.
27. Separate GitHub push from production deploy and verify both independently.
28. Post-deploy smoke both normal and compact/cache paths where used.

## Revised Strategy

A measured rolling reconstruction: discover → classify → rank → claim safe family → full-file rewrite → reread → family tests → browser → performance → global rerun → repeat. GitHub/deploy only after the sitewide ledger reaches a release-safe state.

## NEXT_ACTION

Write the improved Phase Two execution plan, then a final Phase Three critique with at least thirty additional safeguards.
